summary: This program prints the word "Hello" three times using a for loop instead of three separate print statements.

lines.text: This is the loop's instruction to repeat the indented code three times. Changing the 3 to 100 would print "Hello" a hundred times, which is where loops start saving you real work.
The variable i holds the current count on each pass, starting at 0. This program never uses i, but the loop still needs somewhere to keep track of where it is.
The indentation is what puts this line inside the loop. Without those spaces, Python would treat it as code that comes after the loop and print "Hello" only once.
